page: Amazon Web Services hpc7g.8xlarge is a high performance computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton processor family. It features 32 dedicated physical cores using the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture clocked at 2.6 GHz, running one single thread per physical core without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 128 GB of RAM, equating to an even 4.0 GB per core ratio. Cache configuration includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache.

Hardware accelerators are absent, with 0 GPUs provisioned, and the instance includes no local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures. In exchange, hpc7g.8xlarge provides a high-throughput network interface rated at 200 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations reflect top-tier memory subsystem throughput, scoring 3115.3 on PassMark Memory (top 10%) alongside large-block uncached read speeds of 249.58 GB/sec and write speeds of 105.6 GB/sec (top 25%). Multi-core execution ranks high in Geekbench (17579.0) and PassMark physics testing (6741.7).

Cost efficiency is optimized for scale-out parallel workloads through dedicated physical execution pipelines and significant memory bandwidth without paying for unneeded local disks or accelerator silicon. The primary tradeoff stems from the absence of embedded disks and reduced performance in massive large language model prompt ingestion (5.69 tokens/sec for 70B models). The instance is engineered for tightly coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD), molecular dynamics, weather simulation, distributed scientific modeling, and network-bound high-performance computing clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc7g.8xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented instance powered by an arm64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The instance delivers 32 single-threaded physical cores, 128 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core), and a high-throughput baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps on the Nitro hypervisor. It omits hardware GPUs and onboard local storage in favor of massive network connectivity and exceptional memory throughput. Benchmark profiles confirm top-tier memory performance, achieving 249.58 GB/sec uncached reads and a top-10% PassMark memory score of 3115.3, alongside robust multi-core physics and compute scores. With dedicated single-threaded cores that minimize jitter, the hpc7g.8xlarge is purpose-built for scale-out high performance computing tasks, including distributed scientific simulations, computational fluid dynamics, weather forecasting, and tightly coupled parallel computational workloads.
